newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed after slow deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed after slow deal.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed after a slow trading day, with most buyers remaining uncertain over market outlook in the near-term.
Dealers said a firmer close in Tokyo helped RSS rubber prices to end up but SMR grades were down slightly at close.

Uncertainty over weather conditions also kept players at the sidelines. Dealers said buyers were looking for more attractive levels, but prices were expected to remain at current levels in anticipation of supply shortages.
"Weather is another factor. Some rains in the northern parts of the country have slowed down supplies," one dealer said.
There was some Japanese interest in the morning for SMR grades of rubber but dealers said business was slow.
Traders offered the SMR CV at 366 cents, SMR L at 346, SMR 5 at 323, SMR 10 at 312, SMR 20 at 310 and drum latex at 237.
December RSS Ones buyer ended a cent up at 319.50 cents ($1.27) a kg but December SMR 20 eased half a cent to 311.
The INRO five-day average was 244.45 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 18 from 244.71 on Nov 15. The daily indicator was 244.34 against 243.87.
